title: Another Street Fighter HD?  Not exactly
author: Fantastic-Jeweler781
selftext:
This project isn't exactly about developing the game itself. What's being developed here is essentially a wrapper program that runs on top of an emulator, with the original ROM running in the background.

The program interprets the instructions that determine what should appear on screen and replaces the original graphics with new ones. The result is a visually updated version that preserves the exact 1:1 gameplay of the original arcade game, with no additional input lag.

I know projects like MUGEN, as well as SF2 HD Remix and Ultra, already exist, offering high-resolution graphics and visual improvements. However, none of them truly recreates the original gameplay exactly as it was, down to its bugs, glitches, and quirks.

For the average player, these versions might be perfectly fine, but for competitive players, they're simply not the same. I'm talking about people who count frames to execute their combos, understand hitboxes, input buffers, exploits, and obscure hidden mechanics, and have been playing these games for decades. For them, even the slightest change in gameplay is immediately noticeable. They tend to instinctively reject anything that deviates from what they know, at least in gamplay.

(Not that I'm one of them. I'm actually pretty terrible at the game, but I have friends who compete at the national level.)

I showed the preview to one of my friends, who is arguably one of the best KOF '94 and '95 players in the world (no kidding!), and he got really excited about it. So much so that he suggested I do the same thing with those classic SNK games and even offered to organize a crowdfunding campaign within the community to support the project.

I actually loved the idea. The problem is that this whole thing has turned out to be considerably more expensive and time-consuming than I originally anticipated. I'm already using top-tier subscriptions to both Claude and ChatGPT, leaving my PC running for days at a time, and after an entire week of work, Claude estimates we're only about 67% done with the game.

Still, it's been a really fun project, and once it's finished, I plan to release it for free.

As for King of Fighters, that's a whole different beast. Those games are significantly more complex than the old Street Fighter II: Champion Edition, and tackling one of them would be a much bigger undertaking.

So, for now, I think I'll just focus on finishing this project. Maybe at some point I'll put together a small KOF proof of concept, just one stage and one character, to see how far I can push the idea without committing to an entire game.

And perhaps I'll leave it at that.

Then again, that's pretty much how this whole Street Fighter project started in the first place.

So... who knows?

comments.body: These are not visual improvements at all, Pixel art is what people love about this era of games

replies.author: Fantastic-Jeweler781
replies.body: Well. the people who I talked and is very very profesional at playing this game aren't thinking the same, they offered me money!. lol,  but i'm not sure that's the type of task that i wanted to do, this was just an experiment that i want to finish

replies.author: KS-Wolf-1978
replies.body:
Not everyone.

I was a teenager in the ZX Spectrum, Atari and Amiga era.

As the technology progressed and common people could afford PCs with the new SVGA monitors (1280x1024 on a 15" CRT looked really good), me, my cousins and friends were like "Look at this, you can't even see the pixels anymore, this is so great !"

We were that sick and tired of the pixels everywhere.

Then the HD and FullHD became available...

replies.body:
hey, I like pixels too...  but took this task as a technical challenge, and I like it,

replies.body:
Liking pixels in 2026 would make much more sense to me if we were talking about the proper pixels - the flickering glowing blobs you could see on a CRT, not the modern perfect squares.

Yes, i know we have solutions to emulate that, but almost no one uses them in this sub.
